newsitem.title: USA: Calif floods may not dampen 1997 cotton plantings.
newsitem.headline: Calif floods may not dampen 1997 cotton plantings.

text.p: The devastating floods that soaked much of California this winter are not expected to cut cotton output in the nation's second-largest cotton-producing state, industry sources said.
Acreage could even increase slightly in the 1997/98 season, they said, due to planting delays in winter crops such as alfafa, tomatoes and garbanzo beans.

"It's getting too late to plant some of these things," Jarral Neeper, an analyst at Modesto, Calif-based Calcot Ltd, said. "We may actually see a slight increase in acreage from the simple fact that the winter crops are not able to get in the ground."
California's cotton crop is planted between mid-April and the first week in May.

So far, about 30,000 acres to 50,000 acres out of the 1.65 million acres planted last year remain flooded, Neeper said. The U.S. Department of Agriculture will issue the season's first official planting intentions survey March 31.
Market sources anticipated a reduction in California cotton before the floods due to higher competing crop prices. Now, growers who had planned to switch to other crops may be forced to plant cotton.
Joe Bruce of Bakersfield, Calif-based Bruce Cotton Co said some of his clients plan to double their cotton acreage because the ground has been too wet to plant grain.
"There may be less of a decrease than if it had been a nice clear winter," Neeper said.
While losses may be minimal at this point, growers fear that a bout of warm rain at high elevations, which would melt snow and deluge fields with more water, could damage several thousands of acres.
The USDA said in its February report released Wednesday that flood damage varied widely, with some fields suffering total losses and others showing little water damage.
Heavy damage to the farm infrastructure including buildings, equipment, land, irrigation systems and private levees was reported, the USDA said.

The USDA put California's cotton crop at 2.624 million bales 1996/97, compared with 2.452 million bales last year. Growers say the crop remains mostly unharmed as most of the cotton has already been picked.
